raw_comment: In India, substance abuse among children is becoming a serious concern, affecting not only their health and education but also their future. Children may be drawn towards drugs due to peer pressure, family problems, neglect or simply the easy availability of such substances. What may begin as curiosity or an attempt to fit in can gradually become a serious problem. From a legal perspective, children need more than punishment. Articles 21, 39(e) and 39(f) of the Constitution emphasise their dignity, safety and healthy development. The NDPS Act, 1985 addresses illegal drugs and trafficking, while the Juvenile Justice Act, 2015 focuses on care, protection and rehabilitation. Therefore, while those who supply or exploit children must be held accountable, children affected by substance abuse should receive proper counselling, treatment and support to rebuild their lives.
